historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Post-disposal revenue CAGR FY2019-FY2025 (5.7%, asset-light era, through COVID and recovery) tempered to 5.0% for the near-term base path; cross-checked against CMD targets (RevPAR +3-4% plus NUG +3-5% => fee growth 6-10%) and the FY2026 run-rate (+4% reported after FX).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (ordinary shareholders' equity ex-hybrids, 3,293 at Dec-2025) CAGR is negative over 5 years and diverges >30% from revenue/EPS: EUR 2.3bn of buybacks FY2019-FY2025, COVID losses in FY2020-21 and hybrid issuance make book value meaningless as a growth anchor for a capital-returning franchisor. Not used.
historical_growth.notes: FY2014-FY2018 excluded (owned-hotel revenue base, AccorInvest disposal, FY2018 EUR 2.2bn disposal gain). revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020 base, 1,621) is COVID-distorted and shown for completeness only; the 6yr FY2019-based figures are the comparable series. eps_5yr_cagr is null because the FY2020 base is negative (-7.71); FY2025 EPS 1.61 (URD, after EUR 64m hybrid coupons) is depressed by EUR 63m other expenses and the Essendi loss share (adjusted EPS 1.84 vs 1.58). fcf_3yr_cagr is null because FY2021 owner FCF was negative (-357); FY2022->FY2024 owner FCF (Metrics FCF less SBC, 357 -> 399) grew 5.7%/yr; fcf_5yr_cagr uses FY2019 493 -> FY2024 399 on the same basis. FY2025 statement-basis owner FCF 613 - 41 = 572. Accor's own recurring FCF: 614 (FY2024) -> 632 (FY2025). Income-statement history is unchanged by the URD, so the CAGRs are unchanged.

scenario_narratives.base: Accor delivers the lower-middle of its 2023-27 CMD algorithm: RevPAR +2.5-3.5%, NUG ~3.5%, M&F fees +6-7% cc, Services to Owners roughly break-even-to-positive, recurring EBITDA +7-9%/yr to FY2028 then mid-single-digit; consolidated margin drifts from 21.3% (FY2025) to 25% by FY2034 as fees outgrow pass-through revenue. Cash is returned via buybacks (flat count) and a rising dividend; the Essendi stake is monetised near book. Risks priced in weights rather than WACC.
scenario_narratives.bull: Luxury & Lifestyle (Ennismore, Raffles/Fairmont/Orient Express) keeps compounding fees at 12%+ cc, NUG runs 4.5-5% on a pipeline growing ~10%/yr, the franchise pivot lifts fee margin and cuts capex, Middle East recovers in 2027; margin reaches 28% by FY2035 and the exit multiple is a quality-franchisor 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027-28 downturn: RevPAR falls ~5%, openings are deferred, owner support (key money, guarantees) rises, Lifestyle demand proves more cyclical than economy, FX (USD/AUD/TRY) stays a headwind; margin troughs at 19% and recovers only to 21.5%, growth settles at 2-2.5%, exit multiple 14x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Accor as the fee stream it has become since the AccorInvest disposal: unlevered owner FCF built from a consolidated EBITDA margin that expands with fee mix, with SBC expensed, lease cash charged in the flows, NCI leakage charged in the tax line, hybrids treated as debt and the equity-accounted Essendi/Kasada stakes added at book because their income is outside the flows. Risk is charged once, in the scenario weights (25/50/25), with a single EUR-built 8% WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: RevPAR cyclicality and geopolitics: FY2026 guidance is conditional on no further UAE deterioration; a European recession would push RevPAR negative as in the bear case.
Fee-margin mix: the base case relies on M&F fees outgrowing pass-through Services-to-Owners revenue; if reimbursed costs and SMDL scale faster, consolidated margin stalls near 22%.

Essendi disposal: EUR 846m book stake under MoU with undisclosed price; EUR 1,405m of equity-accounted investments sit in the bridge at book (~EUR 6.0/share), so a 25% haircut on Essendi alone is ~EUR 0.9/share.
NCI leakage: Ennismore's 38% minority grows faster than the group; the 6.5pp leakage assumption may prove light if Lifestyle keeps outgrowing economy.
FX: ~40% of fees in USD-linked and EM currencies; FY2025 reported EBITDA growth was +7% vs +13% at constant currency.
Terminal value is ~60% of EV at 18x owner FCF; at 14x the base IV falls materially (see sensitivity grid).
Share count: the 2026 EUR 450m buyback at ~EUR 45 retires ~10m shares (4%) after the 31-Dec-2025 count used here; it is value-neutral at market only if the shares are bought near intrinsic value.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 consolidated revenue (FY2025 URD income statement; unchanged from the Feb-2026 results presentation). Includes M&F fees 1,428, Services to Owners (SMDL + reimbursed costs) and Hotel Assets & Other; pass-through reimbursed costs carry ~zero margin, which is why the consolidated EBITDA margin is ~21% while M&F margin is 72%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 31-Dec-2025 from the FY2025 URD: 234,707,316 issued shares (note 13, AC.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:28858; equity statement :26185; share capital EUR 704.1m at EUR 3 par), ZERO treasury shares ('At December 31, 2025, Accor did not hold any treasury shares', :32696), plus 373,249 dilutive potential shares (IFRS treasury-stock method on unvested performance shares, note 13 :28986; 4,097,260 performance shares outstanding gross, :27229). Replaces the prior indirectly-derived 234.0m estimate. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The EUR 450m 2026 buyback (EUR 698m total return YTD-2026) is value-neutral at market price and is not netted against the Dec-2025 net debt, so count and debt are on the same date.
inputs.net_debt_note: 31-Dec-2025 FY2025 URD note 11.2.1 (:28154-28175): gross financial debt 3,663 (bonds 2,853, NEU CP 398, overdrafts 22, other bank 249, other financial debts 134, derivatives 6) LESS financial assets 1,239 (cash 1,205 + derivative assets 34) = 2,424 ex-lease. Reported Group net financial debt 3,064 = 2,424 + lease liabilities 639; leases are EXCLUDED here because lease cash is charged in the flows (treatment B). Prior build estimated leases at ~690 against the presentation's 3,064, giving 2,374; the actual 639 raises ex-lease net debt by 50. Hybrids are NOT in reported net debt and are deducted separately in equity_bridge.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Both 31-Dec-2025, FY2025 URD balance sheet (:26053 non-current financial debt 3,116 + :26062 current 547 = 3,663; cash :26026 1,205). total_debt - cash = 2,458; net_debt is 34 lower because the net-debt note also nets derivative financial assets (34). In H2-2025 Accor issued EUR 600m 8y 3.50% and EUR 500m 7y 3.625% bonds (bond cash flows +443 net of redemptions, :28188).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Accor 'recurring free cash flow' FY2025 EUR 632m (kpis RecurringFreeCashFlow; presentation p.13: EBITDA 1,201 - cost of net debt 65 - cash tax 202 - lease repayments 113 + non-cash 62 - recurring capex 230 - WC 20). It is levered and post-lease-principal, consistent with lease treatment B; last_fcf = 632 - 41 SBC = 591 is the owner-basis anchor. The statement-basis core_metrics free_cash_flow 613 (OCF 810 - capex 197, FY2025 URD cash-flow statement) is pre-lease-principal (113, :26124) and uses PP&E/intangible capex only (key money sits outside that line), so it is not comparable; it is recorded in Metrics.csv, not used here. Projections are unlevered and built from components, not from either anchor.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net-debt company; interest on the EUR 1.2bn cash (kpis InterestIncome 41) is netted inside 'cost of net debt' and the component build is unlevered, so nothing to strip.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD cash-flow statement / equity statement 'Share-based payments' EUR 41m (AC.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:26176, :26986); FY2024 EUR 41m (FY2024 URD :25709). Replaces the prior estimate of 42. All plans at 31-Dec-2025 are equity-settled (:27204) with no net-share-settlement tax, so no equity-award tax uplift.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share repurchases EUR 452m (kpis ShareRepurchases, URD cash-flow statement; presentation rounded to 440) + dividends paid EUR 327m (kpis DividendsPaid, incl. minorities; ordinary dividend ~303). 10,294,197 shares cancelled in 2025 (:25811). Buyback funds the flat count; it is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 for every anchor (FY2025 URD consolidated balance sheet and notes 7, 9, 11, 13): gross debt, cash, derivative assets, lease liabilities, hybrids, NCI, equity-accounted investments, share count. Supersedes the prior mix of Dec-2025 presentation net debt and Jun-2025 interim balance-sheet items.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.8%, ERP 5.5%, levered beta ~1.3 for a hotel franchisor/manager => cost of equity ~10.0%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.0% (Accor's stated average cost of debt, FY2025) => ~2.25% after tax; market cap ~EUR 10.5bn vs net debt + hybrids ~EUR 3.4bn => D/V ~25%; WACC = 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.25 x 2.25 = 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and geopolitical risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate. Unchanged in this update.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash = principal 113 (:25417) + interest 29 (:27984) = 142, 2.5% of revenue, deducted inside owner EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities EUR 639m at 31-Dec-2025 (:28169; Dec-2024 755) are EXCLUDED from net_debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 330 total less ~115 ROU => ~215, 3.8% of revenue; FY2024 341 less 123 ROU = 218) so the lease is charged once and cash-tax EBIT is not understated. The 2.5% year-1 lease charge was set before the URD and the actual 142/5,639 = 2.5% confirms it; path unchanged.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: minority interests (Ennismore 38% minority, others; book EUR 432m at 31-Dec-2025 = TotalEquityInclMinorities 4,717 - Group share 4,285, :26051; was 421 at Jun-2025; P&L share EUR 50m FY2025 = ~6.2% of owner EBIT) are folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-plus-NCI leakage rate (~25% cash tax + ~6.5pp NCI = 31.5% base). No NCI deduction in the bridge, so the Dec-2025 book value does not enter the valuation. Calibration: FY2025 owner EBIT ~800 x (1-0.315) = 548 vs adjusted attributable net income 504 + after-tax interest ~71 - after-tax SBC ~29 = 546. Ties. Evidence considered and NOT acted on: kpis CashTaxesPaid FY2025 is 214 (statement basis) vs 202 in the recurring-FCF table, i.e. 26.8% of owner EBIT; the 12 gap is non-recurring tax on disposals. The 31.5% path would move only if FY2026 statement cash tax again exceeds ~27% of owner EBIT.
inputs.hybrid_treatment: EUR 991m perpetual subordinated bonds at 31-Dec-2025 (FY2025 URD balance sheet :26049; unchanged from Jun-2025 after the Jan-2025 EUR 148m repurchase; Dec-2024 1,148) are IFRS equity but economically debt (coupons EUR 64m FY2025, :28970, paid out of equity, excluded from EBITDA and from the flows). Deducted in equity_bridge as debt-like; this is the same basis as Accor's own EPS, which subtracts hybrid coupons. Ordinary shareholders' equity ex-hybrids is 3,293 (kpis OrdinaryShareholdersEquity).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035) because the EBITDA margin is still ramping with the fee-mix shift. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in flows, matching-asset rule for equity-accounted stakes, hybrids as debt). Accor is an asset-light hotel manager/franchisor after the 2018-19 AccorInvest (now Essendi) disposal; FY2014-FY2018 figures are not comparable and FY2020-21 are COVID outliers, so every anchor is FY2019 or FY2022-FY2025. UPDATE 2026-10-25 (same day as the first build): the FY2025 URD has been extracted and adjudicated, so every balance-sheet anchor is now the audited 31-Dec-2025 figure and the share count is exact; revenue 5,639 / EBITDA 1,201 / EBIT 871 / net income 449 are identical to the presentation, so NO operating driver (growth, margin, SBC%, lease%, D&A%, capex%, tax+NCI%, WACC, terminal) was changed in any scenario. Price is the last regular close before the valuation date (Friday 2026-10-23); not an after-hours print, and the market has not traded since the prior build. Essendi stake (book 846 at Dec-2025): MoU for sale signed Q1-2026, 'on track' at Q3-2026, price undisclosed in the folder; carried at book in the bridge.
inputs.fy2026_guidance: Q3-2026 release (Oct-2026): FY26 recurring EBITDA upgraded to EUR 1,270-1,285m (incl. ~EUR 10m FX headwind), RevPAR L/L at the high end of +2.0-2.5%, NUG +3.0-3.5%, assuming no further UAE deterioration (UAE RevPAR -26% in Q3-26). YTD-9M revenue 4,263 (+3.6% reported, +4.6% cc); Q3 +9.8% reported. CMD 2023-27 targets: RevPAR +3-4% CAGR, NUG +3-5%, M&F revenue +6-10% cc, recurring EBITDA +9-12% cc CAGR, FCF conversion >=55%, ~EUR 3bn shareholder return.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance; a 2027-28 travel downturn (European recession, Middle East conflict spreading beyond the UAE, USD weakness) takes RevPAR negative for a year, NUG slips to 2-2.5% as owners defer openings, key money per signing rises to defend pipeline, margin falls back to 19% and recovers only to 21.5%; the Essendi sale closes below book (not modelled in the bridge, which is shared). Cap 14x is a mid-cycle cyclical multiple. Unchanged in the 2026-10-25 URD update.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +4.0%: 9M revenue +3.6% reported with Q3 at +9.8% and FX headwind fading (FY2026 revenue ~5,865). FY2027 +5.5% as the CMD 2023-27 fee algorithm (RevPAR +3-4%, NUG +3-5%) runs through a full year; then decays 5.0 -> 2.5 as NUG normalises and the franchise pivot in mature markets trims fee per room. Unchanged in the 2026-10-25 URD update.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 21.8% = guidance midpoint EUR 1,278m on ~5,865 revenue. Expands ~50bp/yr early as high-margin M&F fees (72% EBITDA margin, growing 6%+ cc) outgrow pass-through Services-to-Owners revenue and the loss-making Holding line is held flat; plateaus at 25% from FY2034. Peer asset-light franchisors run 30%+ on fee revenue but Accor's consolidated base includes ~EUR 1.3bn of reimbursed costs and the owned/leased HA&Other hotels. Unchanged.
base.cash_tax_rationale: 31.5% = ~25% cash tax (FY2025 recurring cash tax 202 on ~800 owner EBIT; statement-basis 214 incl. non-recurring; FY2024 23%; French statutory 25.8% plus withholding on international fees) + ~6.5pp NCI leakage (Ennismore 38% minority et al.: EUR 50m FY2025 on ~800 owner EBIT = 6.2%, drifting up as Lifestyle outgrows the group). See inputs.nci_treatment. Unchanged.
base.capex_rationale: Recurring investment incl. key money EUR 230m FY2025 (4.1%) vs statement PP&E+intangible capex 197 FY2025 / 293 FY2024; 4.5% sits above the recurring figure to allow for key money and development spend outside the capex line, easing to 4.2% as the franchise pivot reduces key money intensity. D&A ex-ROU 3.8% below capex, consistent with a growing fee network. Unchanged.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8%/2.5% implies 18.6x FCF; the 18x cap binds marginally. 18x owner FCF is below what listed asset-light hotel franchisors have commanded through a cycle (20-25x) and above Accor's own current ~17x recurring FCF, so the terminal is roughly a no-re-rate assumption. Unchanged.

bull.narrative: Top of the CMD range: RevPAR +4%, NUG 4.5-5% with the pipeline (+9.5% yoy) converting, Luxury & Lifestyle fees compounding 12%+ cc, Middle East normalises in 2027, SMDL margin reaches 10%, Holding costs flat; margin reaches 28% by FY2035; Essendi proceeds and franchise-pivot asset sales fund buybacks at market (value-neutral here). Cap 20x reflects a quality-franchisor exit multiple. Unchanged in the 2026-10-25 URD update.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: hotel demand is cyclical, a Middle East conflict is live in 2026 (UAE RevPAR -26% in Q3-26, guidance explicitly conditional on no further deterioration), ~40% of fees are USD-linked, and FY2025 EPS was already hit by other expenses and the Essendi loss share. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once: top-of-range NUG, Lifestyle fee growth sustained at 12%+, margin to 28%, and a benign macro. Base 50%: the CMD algorithm has been met or beaten in FY2024-25 and FY2026 guidance was upgraded in October 2026. Weights unchanged in the 2026-10-25 URD update.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
